name: Om Power Transmission Ltd
title: Om Power Transmission Ltd - 544750 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Om Power Transmission Q4 FY26 revenue rose 67.2% YoY to INR 174.62 crores; FY26 order book hit a record INR 621 crores.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 174.62 crores, up 67.2% YoY and 68% QoQ, with EBITDA margin of 13.10% versus 17.50% a year earlier. FY26 revenue grew 60.7% to INR 449.16 crores, PAT rose 81.2% to INR 40.02 crores, and ROCE was 44%. Year-end unexecuted order book reached a record INR 621 crores (book-to-bill 1.38x), and management guided to roughly 50% growth in FY27. This was the company's maiden earnings call following its April 2026 listing.

financial_highlights.change: vs 17.50% in Q4 FY25 and 12.51% in Q3 FY26
ROCE 44% in both FY26 and FY25

segments.name: Transmission line EPC
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 51.61% of FY26 revenue; INR 449 crores of the INR 621 crores order book. Company has erected over 1,000 circuit km since incorporation.

segments.name: Substation EPC
segments.commentary: 21.86% of FY26 revenue; INR 140 crores of order book. Covers AIS and GIS up to 220 kV with SCADA monitoring.

segments.name: Underground cabling
segments.commentary: 19.32% of FY26 revenue but only INR 10 crores (about 2%) of order book; management said existing UG projects are executed and a pipeline is building, mainly GETCO tenders.

segments.name: Operation and maintenance
segments.commentary: 7.21% of FY26 revenue; INR 21 crores of order book. Operates more than 100 substations and more than 400 km of transmission lines under long-term contracts.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of around 50%, matching the last three fiscals' pace per CFO Chetan Modi.
Sustained EBITDA margin of 12% to 13% and PAT margin of 8% to 9%.
Gross profit margin range maintained at about 23% to 25%.
Seasonality: H1 about 35% and H2 about 65% of the year.
Order inflow to be kept in line with targeted revenue growth; not necessarily 50%, depends on bid selection and win rate.
Expected entry into DISCOM distribution work with margins of about 12% to 13%; tender result due next month.
capex_capacity: Technical capability has moved from 66 kV to 400 kV for transmission lines and up to 220 kV for substations (AIS and GIS); underground cabling up to 220 kV.
Largest project to date: Dholera 400 kV GIS substation and multiple 400 kV transmission lines across the river, combined value about INR 200 crores, with pile foundation work.
Planned use of part of IPO proceeds for long-term working capital to fund bid deposits, performance guarantees and mobilisation.
Entering 11 kV distribution work over the past two years; no 765 kV experience or order book yet, though GETCO plans 765 kV.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of about INR 615 crores in FY26, the highest ever; PSUs are 82% of the order book and private clients 18%.
Gujarat is 82% of order book; new states are Rajasthan, Punjab and Dadra Nagar Haveli, with 3-4 more states being explored.
Tender pipeline above INR 900 crores as of March 31, 2026; management cites a 30-40% win ratio.

Order book was about INR 745 crores at December 2025 per RHP, with a GETCO order of about INR 45 crores received end-April 2026 per analyst's calculation (management confirmed the ~INR 665-670 crore total).
Price variation clauses in almost all POs pass through raw-material price increases; margins differ by project, with specialised pile foundation work carrying separate margin levels.
Management says it pre-orders routine items such as insulators and breakers to manage supply shortages.

qa_highlights.question: How fast will the INR 620 crore order book execute and what FY27 growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution timeline is 12-24 months, averaging about 18 months. CFO said FY27 would match the last three years' performance, i.e. around 50% growth.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling T&D material shortages and price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Materials are ordered as soon as an LOI arrives, and routine items are bulk-booked in advance. Almost all POs have price variation clauses that compensate cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why has underground cabling share fallen, and is the company deprioritising it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing UG projects were completed on time and more UG tenders are in the pipeline, mainly GETCO. Growth is expected from both UG and overhead lines.

qa_highlights.question: Why is private-sector revenue share falling (35% in FY23 to 15-16% in FY25)?
qa_highlights.answer: Company only takes private projects that meet its margin threshold. Overhead transmission is its core business, with 66 kV and above focus.

qa_highlights.question: What are the win ratio, order pipeline and margin expectations for new states?
qa_highlights.answer: Win ratio on the INR 900 crore pipeline is 30-40%. Margins in new states may be somewhat lower, but management expects to win at similar EBITDA. Guidance is 12-13% EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the working capital cycle stay around 75 days, and what is retention money?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 80% of RA bills are paid within 30 days, with the balance tied to erection and final completion. Retention of about INR 66 crores was outstanding at March 2026.

risks_watch: FY27 growth of 50% depends on converting the pipeline at a 30-40% win ratio; order inflow was slowing per the analyst's comparison with the RHP figure.
Underground cabling order book is only about 2%-3% of the total, against 19% of FY26 revenue.
Entry into 765 kV, distribution and new states carries execution and margin risk, with no current 765 kV orders.
Retention money of about INR 66 crores (March 2026) ties up working capital.
Q4 margin fell YoY to 13.10% from 17.50%; management points to quarterly lumpiness and asks investors to track trailing four-quarter averages.
Raw-material and equipment shortages, though management says price variation clauses currently protect margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on growth and order visibility, with management repeatedly guiding to about 50% FY27 growth. Answers on underground cabling, private-sector share and 765 kV were brief and deflecting, and some answers, such as the DISCOM margin, were given without detail.
key_quotes: Whatever historical performance we have shown in the last three fiscals, with the same performance we will grow in this fiscal '27 as well.
We are expecting to maintain an EBITDA between 12% to 13% and PAT margin of 8% to 9%.

adds.what: Dholera 400 kV GIS substation and multiple 400 kV transmission lines (largest project to date, ~INR 200 crore value; existing project, not new company capacity)

growth.why: Management guides ~50% FY27 revenue growth, matching the last three fiscals, backed by a record INR 621 crore year-end order book (1.38x book-to-bill) and a INR 900+ crore tender pipeline, but no new capacity additions or capex were disclosed and the order book cited is partly unverified against the RHP figure.
